# Bug Catalog: `verify/angler_grunt.gd`

**Generated by /design-tests on 2026-09-06**
**Scope:** `game/goblin.gd` (enemy presentation adapter) and the delivered Angler FBX; one public gameplay class, one asset-import boundary.

## What this file does

`Goblin` is the established display actor for ordinary enemies. This gate keeps its stable gameplay API while proving that Glassgoat's Angler Fish is the actual imported, textured, animated, stage-sized actor behind it.

## Public interface

| Symbol | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `Goblin.new()` | gameplay actor | Creates an ordinary enemy for `Battle` and decoys. |
| `Goblin.play(key)` | animation dispatch | Selects a production idle, movement, attack, hurt, or death action. |
| `Goblin.play_death_fade()` | lifecycle action | Plays death presentation and removes a defeated enemy. |

## IO boundaries

- Asset import: `characters/Angler_Fish.fbx`, including its embedded albedo/emissive images.
- Time: Godot frames advance imported animation playback and death fades.
- Randomness: `Goblin.make_stats()` is intentionally out of scope; this replacement does not alter stats.

## Bug catalog

| # | Bug (one sentence, failure mode) | Blast radius | Plausibility | Test type | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The old Goblin FBX or an empty export remains wired, so normal encounters do not show the Angler. | High — core combat visual remains wrong. | Asset paths are a one-line preload and the first Angler export was empty. | captured contract | open |
| 2 | An imported Angler has no resolved albedo texture and ships white/unstyled. | High — visible art regression on every encounter. | FBX references `.fbm` paths and earlier Tethys delivery lacked textures. | invariant | open |
| 3 | Battle asks for an action key that falls back to idle, so the authored non-humanoid attack/hurt/death motions never play. | High — the validation Glassgoat requested is not actually exercised in combat. | The old asset supplied only idle/walk; Angler uses different take names. | decision-table contract | open |
| 4 | Native asset units produce a giant, tiny, or near-zero combat actor. | Medium — combat framing and target readability fail. | Its raw FBX dimensions differ substantially from the Goblin asset. | invariant | open |
| 5 | Angler inherits the old Goblin's guessed rotation and presents its back to the party. | High — every ordinary fight visibly starts wrong. | `battle.gd` hard-coded `PI` for the retired asset without a model-specific axis check. | directional integration invariant | fixed |

## Test plan

### Bug #1 — replacement identity

- **Test type:** captured contract
- **Description string:** `"ANGLER GRUNT: expected its non-humanoid 19-bone rig — guards against a static or wrong asset"`
- **What it catches:** an empty, unrigged, or accidentally unchanged ordinary-enemy asset.
- **Self-critique:** Cannot pass for a blank stable model because it requires the rig; will not fail under a behavior-preserving import refactor because it asserts the delivered actor contract, not node names.

### Bug #2 — material delivery

- **Test type:** invariant
- **Description string:** `"ANGLER GRUNT: no rendered surface has an albedo texture — guards against the white/missing-texture delivery"`
- **What it catches:** external texture loss or a material import without an albedo texture.
- **Self-critique:** Cannot pass for a white untextured material; will not fail if scene structure changes while a rendered textured surface remains.

### Bug #3 — action mapping

- **Test type:** decision table
- **Description string:** `"ANGLER GRUNT: <key> resolved '<clip>', not an authored <action> clip — guards against a wrong/fallback animation"`
- **What it catches:** each of the five production animation dispatch paths selecting idle/fallback rather than the appropriate authored take.
- **Self-critique:** Cannot pass if a key merely starts any stable animation: it asserts the action semantic in the resolved name. It uses the public `play()` contract, so a compatible refactor passes.

### Bug #4 — presentation scale

- **Test type:** invariant
- **Description string:** `"ANGLER GRUNT: height is not the stage target — guards against a giant/tiny enemy"`
- **What it catches:** loss of runtime AABB normalization.
- **Self-critique:** It asserts battle-visible output (height/radius), not multiplication internals; a differently implemented floor/scale adapter passes.

### Bug #5 — facing direction

- **Test type:** directional integration invariant
- **Description string:** `"ANGLER GRUNT: starts facing away from combat — guards against retaining the Goblin PI rotation"` and `"ANGLER GRUNT: Bite faces away from every target — guards against diver-axis attack aiming"`
- **What it catches:** a stage spawn or production enemy turn whose authored local front points away from the party.
- **Self-critique:** It cannot pass for a back-facing model because it measures the actual actor basis against the actual party centre/target. A compatible refactor may change spawn or aiming code but will retain the same direction.

## Skipped

- Exact bone poses for every clip — deferred to a dedicated animation-deformation test if Glassgoat reports an action is visually static; the five production action mappings give much higher signal for this small ordinary enemy.
- Enemy combat formulas and encounter rates — deliberately unchanged in this asset-only PR and covered by balance/encounter gates.
- World roaming animation — ordinary enemies are combat-stage actors/decoys today; no world enemy movement contract exists to preserve.

## Post-write evaluation

- **Bugs caught:** #3 — before the mapping repair, `swim`, `attack`, `hurt`, and `death` all selected idle because the legacy adapter only supported idle/walk. #5 — the initial battle spawn had a front dot of `-0.954`, confirming the old `PI` rotation showed the Angler's back.
- **Bugs characterized:** #1, #2, #4 — the delivered file imports as the textured, 19-bone, stage-sized Angler.
- **Bugs discovered during writing:** The original texture references look external in the FBX strings, but Godot receives embedded texture data; a filesystem `.fbm` directory is not required.
- **Tests removed:** none.
